1161-program-description: Honours needs a CGPA of at least 3.00.
1162-complementary-courses-18-credits: 6 of research (up to 12 taken, 6 count); 6 of CHEM at 300+, or MATH 315 and 3 of CHEM at 300+; and 6 of CHEM at 400+.
1163-complementary-courses-18-credits: 6 of research (up to 12 taken, 6 count); 9 from the list; and 3 of CHEM at 400+.
1163-program-description: Chemistry fundamentals with physical, computational and math skills for biophysical research in biomedicine and biotech.
1163-program-prerequisites: Honours needs CGPA 3.00. From Foundation: CHEM 110, 120, BIOL 111 or 112, MATH 133, MATH 140/141 or 150/151, PHYS 131/142, or equivalents. Quebec students: a suitable DEC. MATH 150 and 151 replace MATH 222.
1165-about-cognitive-science: The study of intelligent behaviour in humans, animals and machines, across Computer Science, Linguistics, Neuroscience, Philosophy and Psychology. It treats the mind computationally, to explain mental processes and guide intelligent systems. Ask the Program Advisor about the Minor.
1165-program-description: Interdisciplinary study of cognition: intelligence, mind and learning.
1165-complementary-courses-21-credits: At least 6 at 400–500, none from your home department, and at least 9 each in two areas.
1165-linguistics: Any 300–500 level Linguistics course, or the listed ones.
1168-major-and-honours-in-mathematics-an: See p. 1210. Honours students consult an advisor in both departments.
1168-major-and-honours-in-physics-and-co: See p. 1251. Honours students consult an advisor in both departments.
1168-minor-in-cognitive-science: An option for Computer Science students. See p. 1165.
1168-program-description: Get approval from your main program adviser, and ideally talk to a Computer Science adviser. Your selection must be approved before your final term.

COMP 251 opens many upper-level courses, which may require MATH 222, 223 or 323, without credit toward the Minor. Up to 6 credits from high-CS courses elsewhere, approved in advance. Up to 6 may also count toward a Major needing CS.
1169-required-courses-9-credits: If you can already program, skip COMP 202 and add a CS complementary.
1169-complementary-courses-15-credits: From the list and CS courses at 300+, except COMP 396.
1169-program-description: An introduction to CS principles and some sub-areas, at 45 credits, so it can be combined with other concentrations.
1169-required-courses-18-credits: If you know a programming language, skip COMP 202 and add a CS complementary.
1170-program-description: Core programming and software engineering, with practical development options.
1170-required-courses-36-credits: If you know a programming language, replace COMP 202 with CS complementary credits.
1170-complementary-courses-13-credits: 3 and 10 from two lists, or any COMP at 300+ except COMP 396.
1170-program-description-2: The standard School program: broad principles with depth in several areas, leaving room for a minor. 60–63 credits, depending on a COMP 202 exemption.
1171-required-courses-33-credits: If you know a programming language, you can skip COMP 202.
1171-complementary-courses-30-credits: Talk to an adviser first. 6+ from one list, and 3–9 from another including MATH 323 or 340. 6+ at 400+. The rest from CS at 300+ (not COMP 396) and ECSE 539. Check prerequisites for upper-level courses.
1171-program-description: AI and machine learning, foundations and applications. 63–68 credits.
1172-program-description: Biology with the computing and math to manage, analyze and model large biological datasets. 63–74 credits.
1172-program-prerequisites: U0: BIOL 111 and 112; CHEM 110 and 120; MATH 140 and 141 or 150 and 151; PHYS 101 and 102 or 131 and 142. MATH 150–151 replaces MATH 222. Without programming at COMP 202 or 204 level, take one; COMP 204 counts as 202 for COMP 206 and 250.
1173-bio-physical-sciences-core: CEGEP equivalents of MATH 222 or CHEM 212 exempt you; ask an advisor if unsure.
1173-computer-science-and-mathematics: COMP 202 or 204, not both; prior equivalents exempt you.
1173-complementary-courses-27-28-credits: 3–4 and 3–6 from two lists, then 18–21 from the blocks, 9+ at 400+.
1173-computer-science-block: 9–12 from the listed course and COMP at 300+, except COMP 400, 401, 402 and 462, with some at 400+.
1174-program-description: A specialization meeting the CS Major's basics, on game technology, development and design. 62–65 credits, depending on a COMP 202 exemption.
1175-program-description: A more advanced, theory-based Major with a required project. 72–75 credits. Keep CGPA 3.00 throughout and at graduation.
1175-required-courses-46-49-credits: If you know a programming language, you can skip COMP 202. MATH 340 or 350.
1175-complementary-courses-26-credits: 6 from the list and 20 from CS at 300+ (not COMP 396), with some at 500.
1175-program-description-2: Biology, especially molecular, plus computing for large datasets, with more research and advanced courses than the Major. CGPA 3.5; First Class at 3.75.
1176-computer-science-and-mathematics: COMP 202 or 204, not both; prior equivalents exempt you. With COMP 251 instead of 252, take 6+ COMP credits at 400+, 3+ of them at 500+.
1177-complementary-courses-24-credits: 3–6 from a list, then 18–21 from the blocks, 9+ at 400+.
1177-program-description: Broad CS with deep coverage of designing and building software. 60–63 credits, depending on a COMP 202 exemption.
1178-complementary-courses-24-credits: 9 from Groups A and B, 3+ each. 15 from Groups C and D, 9+ from C and 3+ from D.
1178-program-description: A more challenging, research-oriented Major. 72–75 credits, depending on a COMP 202 exemption. Keep CGPA 3.00 throughout and at graduation.
1179-complementary-courses-33-credits: 9+ from Groups A and B, 3+ each. 18+ from Groups C and D, 9+ from C and 6+ from D. 12+ of COMP at 500+.
1180-earth-system-science-interdepartmen: With Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences and Geography. Contact Prof. William Minarik. See p. 1186.
